newsitem.title: USA: Maxxam shareholders to seek redwood sale.
newsitem.headline: Maxxam shareholders to seek redwood sale.

text.p: Maxxam Inc shareholders said on Wednesday they would present a resolution at the annual meeting calling for selling 60,000 acres of redwood forests in northern California.
They accused the company of "pigheadedness" in its failure to divest itself of the controversial Headwaters Forest and five other nearby groves which environmentalists want to save.

"It's important for (Maxxam) management to realize that the shareholders are watching," said Jill Ratner, president of the Rose Foundation, an Oakland, California-based environmental group. The group was to put the resolution up for a vote at Maxxam's shareholders meeting here on Thursday.

Maxxam has urged a vote against, saying it was not in the best interests of shareholders. Maxxam Chairman Charles Hurwitz and his family control 61 percent of the company, making it unlikely the resolution would pass.

Headwaters, the largest stand of old-growth redwood trees still privately owned, is held by Maxxam's Pacific Lumber Co subsidiary. Environmentalists have fought for to save it since Maxxam bought the property in the mid-1980s and stepped up the pace of logging to pay off debt.

The resolution calls upon Maxxam to sell the forests or trade them to the government to end a potential liability connected to 1995 charges that Maxxam, Hurwitz and others mismanaged a Texas savings-and-loan that collapsed in 1988.

Last year, Maxxam reached an agreement with the federal and California governments to sell 5,600 acres of forests in exchange for 7,800 acres of timberland and $300 million in cash and other considerations.
But Ratner accused Maxxam management of making unreasonable demands that have delayed an overall settlement of the redwoods controversy and hurt the company's financial performance.
"Some shareholders fear this represents a certain pigheadedness that's not in the best interest of the company," she said in a news conference.
